metadata.title: Common Shade — Module F: Indonesia
metadata.method: Targeted English/Bahasa primary-source landscape review; selected full legal sections, programme accounts, original study abstracts and official data. Not exhaustive systematic review.
metadata.city_selection: Seven documented heat-concern cities, chosen for evidence and contextual variation. A consistent national most-exposed ranking was not verified; no rank assigned.
metadata.no_endorsement: No organisation is ranked; inclusion implies neither partnership nor endorsement.
metadata.cost_rule: Unknown local package costs and FX are null; no conversion of incompletely specified USD menu into invented IDR price.
metadata.status_rule: Missing facts are recorded as evidence gaps; never treated as proof of absence.
metadata.taxonomy_note: Institution type is one functional website mapping; some actors span multiple roles. Mapping does not change legal identity.
retrieval_limits: NCAP full PDF too large/blocked; official abstract used.
NAP full attachment timed out; UNDP submission account used.
GCF current project/APR pages blocked; AFD programme document used without current disbursement claims.
AC amendment PDF image-only; numerical specifications not reproduced.
Makassar workshop discovery lead could not be opened; excluded from verified claims.

country.name: Indonesia

climate.text: Predominantly hot-humid lowland exposure, with important monsoonal and seasonally drier conditions; elevation and island differences prohibit a single national cooling prescription.
climate.result_basis: Climate-context synthesis; local suitability requires seasonal humidity and water assessment.

night_heat.text: Urban heat storage makes night exposure important; national and city-specific night-health thresholds and comparable city night trends were not established in this snapshot.
night_heat.result_basis: Documented source statement; see review limits

temperature_records.result_basis: measured station summary; BMKG published anomaly retained

heat_context.caveat: Annual mean temperature is not a heat-health threshold; station samples differ and annual variability is not a trend slope.

plans.text: Health-sector RAN MAPIK2025–2030 adopted by Minister of Health Decree HK.01.07/Menkes/777/2025 on 25August2025; official register lists in force. It covers climate-health broadly and does not itself verify a heat-specific municipal activation protocol.
plans.result_basis: Documented source statement; see review limits

plans.text: I-NCAP2024 provides a cooling roadmap combining passive measures, efficiency and refrigerant transition; binding adoption instrument and funded municipal obligations not verified.
plans.result_basis: Documented source statement; see review limits

plans.text: NAP2026–2030 submission is documented by UNDP; full attachment retrieval failed, so its detailed heat commitments and legal force were not appraised.
plans.result_basis: Documented source statement; see review limits

plans.text: KATALIS-HEAT launched July2026 and plans evidence synthesis and municipal heat-health planning; launch is not completed adoption.
plans.result_basis: Documented source statement; see review limits

warning_systems.text: BMKG publishes forecasts, hot-weather explanations and official information through web, social channels and InfoBMKG. Nationwide validated heat-health impact thresholds, automatic cash triggers and offline reach were not verified.
warning_systems.result_basis: Documented source statement; see review limits

warning_systems.text: Pantau Panas Jakarta combines local sensor information and vulnerability mapping; programme page retains BMKG meteorological warning authority. Accessible rendering supplied no live data, so uptime and clinical validity are not established.
warning_systems.result_basis: Documented source statement; see review limits

warning_systems.text: CoCHAP describes developing city thresholds and a tiered system in Medan/Surabaya; historical design cannot be labelled a currently operating warning system.
warning_systems.result_basis: Documented source statement; see review limits

occupational_heat_rules.text: Permenaker5/2018 is in force. Articles7–9 establish assessment/control and include ventilation, drinking water and exposure-time controls; Annex provides ISBB/WBGT limits related to workload and work allocation. No universal ambient-temperature stop-work limit or blanket paid-heat-leave entitlement is inferred.
occupational_heat_rules.result_basis: Documented source statement; see review limits

cooling_and_building_policy.text: Permen PUPR21/2021 covers green-building performance assessment; verify building-class scope and enforcement before applying it to a specific property.
cooling_and_building_policy.result_basis: Documented source statement; see review limits

cooling_and_building_policy.text: ESDM lists energy management, government energy conservation, appliance labels and envelope/HVAC standards; AC procurement must account for amendment134.K/EK.07/DJE/2023, not rely solely on103/2021.

key_gaps: No harmonised nationwide city heat-health exposure ranking verified.
No complete, legally adopted, funded city HAP document retrieved for the seven snapshots; Surabaya drafting is reported separately.
Comparable indoor/night exposure, health outcomes, worker income and actual budget execution remain incomplete in collected evidence.
Grant/loan eligibility, recurrent maintenance and tenant/disability/migrant access require programme-level verification.
collaboration_entry_points_proposed: Contribute local evidence and delivery protocols to the KATALIS-HEAT partners, subject to invitation.
Support PMI/city programmes in Medan and Surabaya with warning-to-action tests and inclusion audits.
Connect low-income housing technical assistance with grants for households unsuitable for debt.
Prepare health-facility/school cooling portfolios with maintenance and power-failure budgets.
country.mapping_note: Taxonomy links and proposed roles are analytical interpretations, not quantified causal or partnership claims.

uncertainty.known: Official heat-health activity, labour rules, cooling policies and implementation examples exist.
uncertainty.inferred: Their connection offers a place-based delivery opportunity.
uncertainty.uncertain: National comparability, enforceability of specific heat actions, local budget execution and health effectiveness.

country.costing_next_step: Obtain date-specific installed IDR quotations, separate energy/water/staff/maintenance/replacement, then use a dated published FX rate. Neither programme size nor loan principal is a universal protection cost.
